code_work.finding: Concurrent deliveries of one research erasure outbox command could both pass the initial inbox lookup and INSERT OR REPLACE distinct receipt IDs under the unique outbox_id constraint, allowing a caller to return a receipt later overwritten by the competing delivery. A further identity-confusion edge case was found: an already-completed inbox row could be replayed with the same outbox_id but a different subject key/version and its receipt returned without identity validation. A deeper race remained: two different subject keys could concurrently reuse the same outbox_id after both read an empty inbox; because deletes preceded the INSERT OR IGNORE, the losing request could erase its own subject's events before the canonical identity mismatch was detected. Another stale-worker downgrade path was identified in the unavailable-RESEARCH_DB branch of processPendingResearchErasureOutbox. Live Express legal-regulatory persistence remains on Firestore; replacing it directly would risk breaking its ten-collection transactional contract.
code_work.fix: Use stable erasure/receipt identifiers derived from outbox_id, INSERT OR IGNORE, and read/validate the canonical committed inbox row before returning. The lifecycle outbox catch path now updates RETRY_PENDING only while the row remains PENDING/RETRY_PENDING; if a competing Worker already completed it, the stale worker reads the durable completed count and treats the item as completed instead of downgrading it.
